speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have a history involving gait and limb ataxia; let's begin by clarifying exactly what symptoms you have experienced and when they started. How would you describe the unsteadiness in your walk, and does it affect one side of your body more than the other?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description; the "drunk" appearance and right-sided clumsiness suggest significant cerebellar dysfunction. Given your significant medical history, have you experienced any episodes of severe headache, vomiting, or vision changes recently?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML).

The combination of subacute cerebellar ataxia in a patient with Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab is highly suggestive of PML, an opportunistic infection caused by the JC virus. Please confirm if you have noticed any new cognitive changes, weakness on the left side, or visual field cuts. I am requesting MRI images of the brain to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST IMAGES: Brain MRI with contrast.
